sections.h2: Your options for selling in Cibolo
sections.html:
Cibolo homeowners usually choose among an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash purchase that leaves the house untouched. Repair needs and your calendar decide.

  • Agent: wide exposure, with showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal to wait through.
  • Do-it-yourself: you handle pricing, negotiation and contract details.
  • Cash purchase: removes repair requests and the loan step, which helps with inherited houses, rentals and deadlines.

A few Cibolo details shape any route: the city's place east of San Antonio, a county line nearby, and a permit office that works through one online portal.

Cibolo lies in the far western corner of Guadalupe County, along FM 78 and FM 1103, with Interstate 10 to the south and Interstate 35 to the north. It is about 13 miles east of the San Antonio metropolitan area and sits in what the city calls the Metrocom, the northeast corner of Bexar County and the southwest corner of Guadalupe County. Schertz, Universal City, Selma, Live Oak, Garden Ridge, Converse and Kirby are neighbors.

The city voted to become an independent township on October 9, 1965, when about 440 people lived here by the 1970 count. An estimated 37,061 lived here by 2023, so many of the lots, surveys and permits you deal with are recent.

Cibolo is in Guadalupe County, but the surrounding Metrocom reaches into northeast Bexar County. Confirm the tax roll for your parcel on your statement before you set a price.

Every Texas district values property on January 1 and mails notices in spring. Bills go out near October 1, and what is still unpaid on February 1 draws a six percent penalty plus one percent interest. The penalty grows a point a month until it reaches 12 percent in July.

A homestead owner receives a $140,000 school district exemption, and that home's appraised value can't rise more than 10 percent a year. A buyer files a new application after closing. For a balance and current rates, ask the county tax office rather than an online estimator.

sections.h2: Permits and the Cibolo building office
sections.html:
The Cibolo Building and Permitting Department handles permits and inspections and asks everyone to apply through the MGO Connect portal. It is at 201 West Loop 539, and the main office number is (210) 658-4175.

Cibolo building office inspection hours and codes
ServiceHours or rule
Building inspectionsMonday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM
Fire inspectionsTuesday and Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM
Permit portalMGO Connect, account required
Codes in force2021 International codes and 2023 NEC, under Ordinance 1475

Find any permit tied to your address and see whether it was closed. The portal has a permit lookup, and the office email is permitting@cibolotx.gov. A deck, pool, new water heater, patio cover or addition with no final inspection is the kind of item that can hold up a title company or a buyer's inspector.

Cibolo enforces the 2021 editions of the International Building, Residential, Energy Conservation, Plumbing, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Swimming Pool and Spa, and Fire Codes, along with the 2023 National Electrical Code, under Ordinance 1475. Local amendments are listed on the city's Codes and Fees pages.

  • Contractors must register before they submit a permit application.
  • An account in the portal is required before any application.
  • Permits, inspections and permit lookups all run through the same portal.

Before starting repairs, ask the office whether the work needs a permit. If you are selling as-is instead, put any unfinished work in writing for the buyer.

The city's FAQ adds detail for homeowners. A shed needs a permit if it sits on a permanent foundation, can't be moved once installed, or exceeds 100 square feet. Water heaters, roof work, replacement HVAC, electrical, plumbing, irrigation and water softener permits can be issued at submittal without plan review. Residential plan reviews may take up to 10 business days, and the city has no process to expedite them.

City Utility Services at Cibolo City Hall, 200 South Main Street, handles water and wastewater accounts, and the city doesn't currently waive deposits or administration fees. Tell your buyer which utility account to open, and close your own as part of the move.

If your land was recently annexed, the city's FAQ cites Texas Local Government Code Chapter 43 and lists what changes: voting rights and representation, public street maintenance, land use and density rules through zoning, and code enforcement. An agricultural exemption can continue while the property keeps qualifying, and the city doesn't expect address changes. A buyer of acreage on the edge of town should ask planning staff how zoning treats the parcel.

Texas puts different clocks on each.

  • Probate: four years from death to probate a will, with court discretion afterward. Heirs may file an affidavit of heirship with the clerk, but a title company is free to refuse it.
  • Tenant: written notice to vacate of at least 3 days, then a justice court case, and a writ of possession no sooner than 6 days after judgment.
  • Foreclosure: a courthouse auction on a first Tuesday; if the lender later sues for a deficiency, it must do so within two years of the sale.

With two or more of these in play, a cash buyer can often work around them, but the title company still needs documents showing who has authority to sign.

sections.h2: Before you list or take a cash offer
sections.html: Look up your permits, confirm your county on the tax statement, and get a payoff figure if there is a loan. Then decide whether repairs are worth doing or whether to sell as-is and disclose what is unfinished.

faqs.a: The city places itself in the far western corner of Guadalupe County, with the surrounding Metrocom area covering northeast Bexar County. Your tax statement shows which appraisal district holds your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I check for an open permit on my Cibolo house?
faqs.a: Use the MGO Connect portal, which has a permit lookup, or contact permitting@cibolotx.gov or (210) 658-4175. Closing any open permit before you list helps the sale move.

faqs.q: Which building codes does Cibolo enforce?
faqs.a: The 2021 International codes and the 2023 National Electrical Code, under Ordinance 1475. The Codes and Fees section of the city site lists local amendments.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1 if unpaid by the end of January, when a penalty plus interest begin to accrue.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Cibolo house without a full probate case?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A muniment of title or small estate affidavit can work when the estate qualifies and a court approves it. A probate attorney can say which route fits your family.
